input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: The Agreement runs on a Product-by-Product/country-by-country basis until the Secondary Royalty Terms expire (13.1), i.e. a multi-year committed term, but Ono's only convenience exit (13.2) does not arise at all until a redacted period after First Commercial Sale of both the Binimetinib and Encorafenib Products, and the notice period is redacted. For the whole development and pre-launch period Ono therefore has no right to terminate for convenience, which is walk-away territory under the rule and fails both the preferred (30 days) and fallback (60-90 days) notice positions since the required notice cannot be verified. There is also no pro rata refund of prepaid amounts. Array's side is already compliant: its only termination rights are for material breach (13.3), bankruptcy (13.4) and Ono's Competing Product breach (8.2), none of which is a convenience right, and our edit records that expressly. We have targeted the preferred level with a single edit to 13.2: the gating trigger is removed, notice is fixed at thirty (30) days, a pro rata refund of prepaid fees is added and Array's lack of a convenience right is confirmed, leaving the rationale-notice requirement and all other termination mechanics untouched. Note (not separately flagged): the Section 8.2 Competing Product tail attaches a post-termination non-compete to an at-will exit during the Initial Royalty Term, and Section 6.1 makes the upfront licence fee non-refundable; neither is an early-termination fee, but the refund wording is drafted to reach only amounts prepaid for post-termination periods.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.

proposal.summary: Make Ono's at-will termination right available from the Effective Date on 30 days' notice with a pro rata refund of prepaid fees, and confirm Array has no convenience termination right.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our convenience exit should not be blocked until a redacted date after First Commercial Sale of both Products, and the notice period should be fixed at thirty (30) days with a pro rata refund of any fees prepaid for post-termination periods. We have also confirmed expressly that Array has no convenience termination right; we can discuss 60-90 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.newText: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement at any time, for any reasons by giving thirty (30) days' advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination, and Array shall refund to Ono on a pro rata basis any fees prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination. Array shall have no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience.
